patterns_detected.description: An entity whose attribute set varies (by type or category, or as attribute rows), read by its key: DocumentDB stores each entity as one document of up to 16 MB with only the fields it has; it has no wildcard index, so each queried attribute needs its own index (Amazon DocumentDB Developer Guide, Quotas and limits; Functional differences).
A grouped aggregate, or one over rows no key anchors, that maps to DocumentDB's aggregation pipeline ($group, $match, $project, $sort).

Queries joining large transactional tables with small reference/lookup tables (country, merchant, payment_type) just to get display names. Embed the few referenced fields directly, especially valuable in DocumentDB, where every $lookup is a read-time join.

anti_patterns_detected.description: Queries joining 3 or more tables. Each join becomes a $lookup stage that reads the joined collection for the documents flowing through it, one stage per collection, with a nested-loop, hash or sort-merge algorithm (Amazon DocumentDB Developer Guide, Functional differences, $lookup); correlated $lookup needs DocumentDB 8.0.2 or later.
anti_patterns_detected.recommendation: Pre-denormalize via Extended Reference Pattern or write-time aggregation. Never chain $lookup operations.

anti_patterns_detected.description: Queries with NOT IN, <>, !=, NOT EXISTS, which map to $ne/$nin/$nor. Query planner version 2 and later use indexes for $ne, $nin and $not, so a negation is no worse on DocumentDB than on an engine where it is rarely index-selective (Amazon DocumentDB Developer Guide, Query planner).
anti_patterns_detected.recommendation: Redesign hot query paths to use positive equality operators ($eq, $in).

pricing_assumptions: Standard storage I/O: $0.2 per million read/write requests

Read I/O: only cache misses billed, at the source's instance-wide buffer-cache hit ratio (99.99993%), not scaled to the target's memory (the source reported no memory size), billed at 99%. At least 1% of every read is billed as a miss.
No backups, snapshots, or data transfer included
